_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and every banned anti-pattern still absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Schema and rationale: docs/reprint-survival.md. Regen steps: cli-factory/saas-alerts/handfixes/regen.sh (re-applies apply_client_patch.py + apply_doc_patch.py).

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard compares trustees by SID, resolving SDDL aliases through the OS, so the built-in Administrator (RID 500, rendered as LA) can save and load credentials
handfixes.why: Press 4.30.2+ creds_perms_eval.go compared the SDDL text of the token file's owner and ACE trustees against the process's SID string. The SDDL converter renders the built-in local Administrator (RID 500) as the alias LA, so that account's own ACE never matched: `auth set-token` exited 1 with `token file DACL grants access to a non-owner principal (LA)` and every read refused the file. Reproduced 2026-10-15 on the published fortinet-cli 0.1.0, installed with the README one-liner on a windows-latest runner (whoami S-1-5-21-...-500). The fix resolves each trustee to its SID (fixed aliases from a table, machine-relative ones like LA through ConvertStringSidToSid, kept only when the converter renders that SID back to the same alias) and compares SIDs. The allow-list is unchanged (current user, BUILTIN\Administrators, SYSTEM): an owner or allow-ACE trustee that is any other principal, a broad group, or unresolvable is still refused. A reprint from an unfixed press silently restores the string compare while unit tests stay green on every non-Windows host.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press defect in internal/generator/templates/cliutil_creds_perms_eval.go.tmpl and cliutil_creds_perms_windows.go.tmpl (unfixed on press main as of 4.33.5). Reported upstream: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5029

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard checks the DACL section's framing, so a NULL DACL is refused in the form Windows actually renders it, flags first (D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL), and DACL text that does not frame as flags plus complete six-field ACEs is refused rather than skipped
handfixes.why: Press creds_perms_eval.go refused a NULL DACL only when the DACL section began with NO_ACCESS_CONTROL. SDDL puts DACL flags (P, AI, AR) first, and a real NULL DACL on Windows Server 2025 renders as O:<owner>D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL (measured on a windows-latest runner, 2026-10-15), so the guard found no ACEs to inspect and accepted a world-accessible token file. That was already a hole for every ordinary account; for the built-in Administrator the owner-alias mismatch happened to refuse it, so resolving LA (windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare) without this fix would have widened the hole. The DACL section's framing is now checked: its flags must be drawn from P/AI/AR/NO_ACCESS_CONTROL, an empty DACL followed by a SACL section ends at that section, and the ACE list must be complete, un-nested (...) groups of exactly six fields. Unknown flags, an unclosed or nested group, stray text, or a wrong field count is refused (fail-closed). ACE flags and rights are not validated; they do not change which principal an allow ACE names.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Same press templates as windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare; reported in the same upstream issue: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5029

handfixes.summary: Respond API calls mint an accesstoken from the partner api_key (POST /respondApi/api/v1/auth), attach it, re-mint once on rejection, and mask every token in output
handfixes.why: The Respond API (spec 2.0.0) requires an accesstoken header minted from the partner api_key; without it every call answers 400 'Only secure origins are allowed' (live receipt 2026-10-14). Press 4.33.5 has no api-key-to-token exchange auth mode, so client.go is hand-patched to call respond_token.go. A reprint re-emits client.go without the hook and every Respond command (rule-triggers, rules, response-actions, contain) silently fails.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Generator auth mode for an api_key -> access-token exchange scoped to a path prefix (cli-factory/saas-alerts/handfixes/patches/saas-alerts-respond-access-token.json)

handfixes.summary: synced events are keyed by _id, else a customer/product/account-scoped eventId, else a content hash
handfixes.why: Reports eventId is the source product's raw id and collides across customers, products and users; the press id override cannot express a prefer-_id fallback chain, so distinct events overwrote each other at sync and triage/cross-tenant undercounted. A reprint restores the generic id extraction.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Ordered id fallback chains (x-resource-id with alternatives) in the generator

handfixes.summary: events sync maps --since to the documented `start` param; rule-trigger sync follows Respond's [ts, id] array cursor as repeated startAfter keys and treats only a literal pagination.hasNextPage:false as the end
handfixes.why: GET /reports/events filters by `start` (date-time), which the press since-detector misses, so incremental sync re-pulled everything. GET /rule-triggers pages with pagination.cursor = [ts, id] passed back as repeated startAfter keys and a nested pagination.hasNextPage flag; generic sync handles only scalar cursors and top-level has_more names, so it stopped after page 1 or pruned rows on an unproven end.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Since detection for `start` date-time params; array cursors and nested has-more flags in generic sync

handfixes.summary: rule-triggers decide, contain and subscriptions health --reenable only preview without --confirm, and the MCP read-only mode treats them as reads only while --confirm is absent
handfixes.why: These three commands change live Respond triggers, Microsoft 365 accounts (block sign-in, expire sessions, reset password) and webhook subscriptions. The preview default and the mcp:read-only-unless-flags annotation are what keep an agent from acting on a customer tenant by accident; governance.md tiers them as writes on that basis. A reprint that loses either turns a preview into a live write.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Novel commands; re-author with the same --confirm contract on any reprint

handfixes.summary: contain refuses a non-Microsoft 365 account and an email that maps to more than one Microsoft 365 account instead of guessing
handfixes.why: Respond response actions run against application MS only. Acting on the wrong account, or on a Google Workspace user that happens to share an email, would block or reset a real person. contain exits non-zero on any unclear case and asks for --org-id/--account-id.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Novel command; re-author with the same refusal on any reprint

handfixes.summary: the MCP server's --transport http bearer token is read through cliutil.EnvOverride, so an unresolved ${user_config.saas_alerts_mcp_http_token} placeholder refuses to start instead of becoming the secret
handfixes.why: The generated requireHTTPCallerToken read SAAS_ALERTS_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN with os.Getenv. The variable is declared as an optional MCPB user_config value, and a host that skips an optional prompt leaves the literal placeholder text in the environment; that text is public (it is in manifest.json), so anyone could authenticate to an HTTP-mode server started that way. Same fix as bitdefender and sophos-central. TestHTTPTokenPlaceholderRefused fails when the read goes back to os.Getenv (proven 2026-10-20).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: the press main_mcp.go.tmpl should read the HTTP token through cliutil.EnvOverride for every connector.

handfixes.summary: every Webhooks API (/outgoingWebhookApi/) response has its subscription `token` replaced with [withheld] in the client's JSON success path, before print, response cache, sync, tail and MCP; the --dry-run request preview of a Webhooks API write withholds the token too; a Webhooks API write whose token is the [withheld] placeholder is refused (dry-run included)
handfixes.why: GET /subscriptions and /subscriptions/disabled return each subscription's token, the string SaaS Alerts attaches to every delivery so the MSP's receiver can authenticate it (webhooks spec 0.9.0, schema Token). Before this fix a sentinel token reached `subscriptions list` output, the MCP saas-alerts_execute result, the HTTP cache files and the local SQLite store (mock receipt 2026-10-20). subscriptions health --reenable sends only enabled plus filter fields, so the blanked value is never written back. Delivery URLs are kept: domain checks need them and SaaS Alerts only delivers to verified domains. TestWebhookTokenNeverLeavesTheClient fails when the hook is removed (proven 2026-10-20).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Generator support for x-secret / writeOnly response fields that are blanked before print, cache and store.

handfixes.summary: an env-sourced SAAS_ALERTS_BASE_URL is marked as an env override in config.Load and configForSave writes the file's own value back, so config.toml never captures the override
handfixes.why: The generated configForSave restored only the env-sourced API key, so `auth set-token` run with SAAS_ALERTS_BASE_URL set wrote that one-run URL into config.toml (reproduced 2026-10-20: base_url = the env value after set-token). After that, unsetting the variable had no effect and every later call sent the saved partner key to the old host. internal/config/env_base_url_test.go fails with the fix removed (proven 2026-10-20). Same generator defect bitdefender and threatdown carry.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Generator defect: configForSave should restore every env-overridden field, not only credentials.

handfixes.summary: --csv, --plain and --quiet output drops terminal control characters (ESC, BEL, C1) from values
handfixes.why: Event fields come from monitored tenants and can be attacker-chosen (a malicious inbox rule or shared file name), and the generated printCSV/printPlain/printQuiet wrote them raw, so a value carrying an OSC 52 or CSI sequence could rewrite the terminal or the clipboard (mock receipt 2026-10-20: ESC and BEL reached --csv and --plain). scrubCell keeps tab/CR/LF for CSV quoting; quiet output uses cliutil.ScrubTerminal. Same fix as bitdefender. TestTabularPrintersScrubTerminal fails with the scrub removed (proven 2026-10-20).

handfixes.summary: stdout and stderr are wrapped in c1EscapeWriter, which rewrites UTF-8 C1 controls (U+0080-U+009F) as \u00XX; isTerminal unwraps it
handfixes.why: encoding/json escapes C0 controls but writes C1 raw, and xterm/VTE act on UTF-8 C1 (CSI, OSC, ST), so a tenant string in --json, --agent or the default pretty-JSON output could drive the terminal. The escape keeps JSON valid and lossless. Ported from bitdefender (adversarial review round 7, 2026-10-19). c1_escape.go is hand-written; root.go wires it in Execute and in the --deliver multiwriter, and helpers.go isTerminal unwraps it so TTY detection is unchanged.

handfixes.summary: rule-triggers list --all follows Respond's [triggeredAt, id] pagination.cursor as repeated startAfter keys and stops on a literal pagination.hasNextPage false, instead of stopping after page 1
handfixes.why: The generic paginatedGet reads only scalar cursors, so --all fetched page 1, printed a truncated event on stderr and returned an un-flagged partial list on stdout with exit 0 (mock receipt 2026-10-20: 2 of 3 triggers). paginationCursorToken now accepts the two-element array (cursorValue owns the rule), the fetch-all GET re-expands it into repeated startAfter keys (replacing any --start-after on the path), and a literal hasNextPage:false ends the walk even though Respond also returns a cursor on the last page. TestRuleTriggersListAllFollowsArrayCursor fails with either change reverted (proven 2026-10-20).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Array cursors and nested has-more flags in the generic paginatedGet (same deferral as sync-events-start-and-respond-array-cursor).

handfixes.summary: triage, cross-tenant, investigate and coverage report synced:false (with a 'the last <resource> sync did not finish' note, and the resource in unsynced_resources) when a checked resource's latest sync attempt did not finish, not only when it was never synced. Only events (the windowed resource) counts an unfinished attempt after a completed one; any resource that stored rows but never finished a sync is reported as unfinished, not as never synced
handfixes.why: In the default auto data source a stale store triggers a bounded, page-capped refresh: one page of the 100 newest events since the last sync. With more new events than that, the store missed every older one, yet triage said synced:true and the digest silently dropped critical alerts for whole customers (adversarial review 2026-10-20, P1; mock receipt: 3 of 4 criticals, synced:true). saasIncompleteResources reads sync_state.last_attempt_complete; a fully fetched refresh still marks the attempt complete (verified), so this does not false-RED a healthy store, and `sync --resources events` closes the gap (verified 180/180). TestSaasIncompleteSyncIsNotSynced fails with the check disabled (proven 2026-10-20). The never-synced remedy also moved from --since 7d to --since 24h because the events search stops at 10,000 rows per sync. Round 2 (2026-10-20): a head-of-list rule-triggers refresh after a full sync made investigate synced:false every 15 minutes, so list resources now count only a never-finished first sync (TestSaasListRefreshAfterFullSyncStaysSynced, TestSaasStartedButUnfinishedIsNotEmpty).

handfixes.summary: a PENDING Respond trigger counts as superseded only by a newer trigger of the same rule for the same organization and accounts
handfixes.why: The Respond spec says only that a manual approval expires 'when the rule triggers again or 12 hours whichever is earlier', without the scope. Keying by rule id alone let one customer's firing mark another customer's live approval expired: rule-triggers queue hid it (expired_count only) and rule-triggers decide skipped it, so a compromised account could stay unblocked (adversarial review 2026-10-20, mock receipt). The narrow key can only err toward showing a trigger Respond already expired, whose approve the API refuses. Widen it only against a live tenant. TestRespondSupersessionNeverHidesAnotherCustomer fails with the rule-only key (proven 2026-10-20).

handfixes.summary: every press auth hint that prints `export SAAS_ALERTS_API_KEY=...` also prints the PowerShell form, and auth setup prints a PowerShell line; the hints name the dashboard button as GET APIKEY, the vendor help's wording
handfixes.why: Windows is the primary MSP platform and the generated hints (auth setup, auth status, doctor auth_hint, the HTML-instead-of-JSON and 401 hints, the placeholder-credential error) were POSIX-only (adversarial review 2026-10-20, P2). Same pattern as backup-radar's auth-hints-windows-twin.

handfixes.summary: a completed events sync records the earliest instant the store covers (saas_events_coverage); triage, cross-tenant, investigate and coverage report synced:false with a 'holds events only from' note when their window starts before it; coverage checks the larger of --silent and its fixed 7-day events_7d window, and remedies render a --since value sync accepts
handfixes.why: synced only said whether a sync ran and finished, never whether it covered the requested window, and incremental syncs only move forward, so after `sync --since 24h` a `triage --since 7d` returned synced:true over one day of a seven-day window (adversarial review round 2, 2026-10-20, P1; mock receipt 20 of 32 events, 7 of 11 criticals). Floor rules: no --since = full history; incremental keeps the floor; an explicit --since at or before the previous watermark extends it; one after the watermark leaves a hole, so the floor restarts. Verified e2e: the 7d gap is flagged, 12h is not, and `sync --resources events --since 7d` closes it. TestSaasWindowOlderThanCoverageIsNotSynced fails with the check disabled (proven 2026-10-20).

handfixes.summary: Unify v2 device syncs (devices, devices-ignored, devices-mapped, devices-unmapped) page with pageSize 1000 and searchAfter = the previous response's meta.sort, sent as repeated searchAfter keys
handfixes.why: The generated sync sent only pageSize=100 with no cursor, so any partner with 100+ Unify devices stopped at page 1 with cursor_unavailable and investigate reported 'no synced devices' forever (adversarial review round 2, 2026-10-20, P1). Manage 1.2.0 documents pageSize max 1000 and searchAfter (string array) = previous meta.sort. The live envelope is unverified (the spec example is a bare array); a bare full page still ends as an unfinished sync, never as complete. Mock receipts: {data, meta.sort} envelope 2500/2500 in 4 requests; bare 700 complete; bare 1000 unfinished. TestUnifyDevicesSearchAfterRepeatedKeys fails with the syncGet expansion removed (proven 2026-10-20).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Generator support for searchAfter-style array cursors taken from a response path.

handfixes.summary: --select on triage, cross-tenant, investigate and coverage (and their missing-store envelopes) always keeps synced and note (plus unsynced_resources for investigate and coverage)
handfixes.why: An agent following the documented `coverage --select customers.customer_name,customers.flags --agent` lost the partial/unsynced signal from stdout (adversarial review round 2, 2026-10-20). The existing --select tests now assert the kept keys.

handfixes.summary: an events sync never resumes a saved offset (it restarts from the top); a sync of ANY resource narrowed by --param/--global-param/--resource-param (including a page-size override) stores its rows but is marked incomplete before reconcile (no prune, no watermark, no coverage floor), on the flat and the dependent path, and the summary counts it as warned; an explicit incremental events sync re-reads saasEventsLateAllowance (6h) before the watermark; parameters a resource requires do not count as narrowing; a filtered walk never saves a resume cursor; the late-event look-back anchors to the last explicit sync's watermark (saas_events_explicit_watermark), which the page-capped auto-refresh cannot move
handfixes.why: Events page by offset over timeSort=desc, so a saved offset from an unfinished sync shifts as new events arrive; resuming it skipped them and the completed resume then advanced the watermark past them (adversarial review round 3, 2026-10-20, P1: 350 of 400 new events stored, synced:true). A filtered sync (Codex 2026-10-20, P1) saved the partner-wide watermark and coverage floor from one customer's events, so triage said synced:true and later incremental syncs never fetched the other customers; with --full it would also have pruned their local rows. TestSaasEventsSyncRestartsFromTop and TestSaasFilteredEventsSyncIsNotComplete fail with either guard disabled (proven 2026-10-20). Codex round 2 (2026-10-20, P1): the guard was events-only, so `sync --resources rule-triggers --full --resource-param rule-triggers:organizationIds[]=ORG_A` pruned other organizations' triggers, and `--param pageSize=100` made a full bare Unify page look terminal; it now covers every resource (TestSaasFilteredFullSyncNeverPrunes fails with the guard disabled, proven 2026-10-20). Adversarial round 4 (P1): events are filtered by event time and SaaS Alerts pulls some late (isLatent), so a sync starting at the watermark never fetched them; TestSaasIncrementalEventsSyncRereadsLateAllowance fails without the allowance (proven 2026-10-20). The page-capped auto-refresh keeps the plain watermark. Adversarial round 5 (2026-10-20, P1): counting required params (events-fileshare startDate/endDate, report organizationIds) made those resources impossible to complete, and an auto-refresh moving the watermark shifted the explicit look-back past late events. Codex round 3 (P1): a filtered --max-pages walk saved a cursor a later unfiltered sync resumed. TestSaasFilteredSyncDropsItsCursor and TestSaasLateAllowanceAnchorsToExplicitSync fail with their fix disabled (proven 2026-10-20).

handfixes.summary: the human output of triage, cross-tenant, investigate, coverage, rule-triggers queue, decide, contain and subscriptions health goes through saasScrubWriter, which drops C0 controls (ESC, BEL...) except tab and newline
handfixes.why: Those renderers interpolate tenant strings (user, customer, rule and device names) and emit no styling, while the root c1EscapeWriter escapes only C1; a name carrying an OSC 52 or CSI sequence could rewrite the terminal or clipboard (Codex 2026-10-20, P1). handfixes.summary: contain accepts a unique Microsoft 365 account from synced rule triggers only when synced users name no different account (or unreadable rows) for the same email
handfixes.why: The trigger resolver returned before the users resolver ran, so an email that is a trigger-backed account at one customer and a synced user at another resolved silently to the first and `contain --confirm` could block or reset the wrong person (Codex round 2, 2026-10-20, P1). Refusing is the safe direction for a lockout; --org-id/--account-id select explicitly. TestContainCrossSourceAmbiguityRefuses fails with the check disabled (proven 2026-10-20).

handfixes.summary: subscriptions and subscriptions-disabled are stored by channelId, not url
handfixes.why: The Webhooks schema identifies a subscription by channelId; several subscriptions can share one receiver url, and keying by url collapsed them into one local row (adversarial review round 4, 2026-10-20; mock: fetched 2, stored 1). Verified: two subscriptions store as ch-0001 and ch-0002.

handfixes.summary: the users dependent sync prunes by the injected parent_id ($.parent_id) and refuses a --global-param/--resource-param that overrides the customerId it sets for each customer

Overriding customerId fetched one customer's users and stamped copies under every other customer (Codex round 3, P1).
